primary_sources.title: Stefan Haller, The Atiyah-Singer index theorem, winter term 2012/13
primary_sources.reviewed: Pages 11-12: Theorem I.3.1, Lemma I.3.2 and Corollary I.3.3 with the parametrix and index-preservation proofs.
primary_sources.use: Standard Fredholm invariance under compact perturbations, applied to the retained curvature operator as a bounded map on its graph domain. No domain or spectrum is imported from an unrelated geometric example.

source_access: Haller's author-hosted PDF was opened directly and the stated proof passages were reviewed. An attempted direct open of Dyatlov-Zworski's larger book PDF failed because the tool rejected its content length; it is not used as the reviewed proof. No downloaded-source digest is claimed.
strongest_comparators: The scalar minimal-domain range theorem has index -1 with shape held as a source; the latest complete thermal Schur theorem controls a variational mixed form. Neither alone supplies the full strong curvature-source feedback after auxiliary shape elimination.
hardest_step: Derive the exact strong trace-density bridge with gauge and volume residual contacts, distinguish D K^dagger from the variational M, and prove relative compactness in the original scalar graph domain. Multiplication by A1 is not claimed compact on physical L2.
new_consequence: The complete auxiliary thermal pair retains index -1 under removal of both outer fast traces, so a nontrivial coupled source compatibility remains even after solving shape. The cokernel dimension may exceed one if a kernel is present.
verification_scope: Exact charged four-dimensional curvature jets test the strong trace-density bridge and nonzero residual contacts. Exact finite-rank modifications of an infinite shift test Schur source signs, compatibility and kernel/cokernel distinctions. The charged infinite-dimensional Fredholm conclusion is an ordinary proof, not a finite-rank numerical certification.
